d: Account-based marketing (ABM) targets a defined list of high-value companies with coordinated sales and marketing. Learn how ABM works in B2B.
An account executive (AE) is the seller who runs qualified deals from discovery to signed contract. Learn what an AE does and how it differs from SDRs.
An agentic workflow is a multi-step process where AI agents plan, use tools and make decisions within defined steps. Learn how it differs from automation.
An AI agent is software built on a language model that plans steps and uses tools to complete a goal. Learn how AI agents are used in sales and marketing.
An AI sales agent is AI software that carries out sales tasks such as research, outreach and follow-up with some autonomy. Learn what they do and their limits.
An AI SDR is software that uses AI to research prospects, write outreach and handle replies. Learn what AI SDRs do and how they differ from a sequencer.
Annual recurring revenue (ARR) is the yearly value of a company's subscription contracts. Learn how ARR is calculated and how it differs from revenue.
An attribution model is the rule for giving credit for a conversion to the touchpoints before it. Learn first-touch, last-touch and multi-touch models.
Average contract value (ACV) is the typical yearly value of a customer contract. Learn how ACV is calculated and why it shapes a go-to-market motion.
B2B SaaS is software sold to businesses as a subscription and delivered over the internet. Learn how the B2B SaaS model works and what it measures.
Backlinks are links from other websites to yours. Learn why backlinks matter for SEO, what makes a good one and how dofollow and nofollow links differ.
Bottom of funnel (BOFU) is the decision stage, where buyers choose a vendor. Learn what BOFU content looks like and why it converts best.
Bounce rate is the share of website sessions that leave without engaging further. Learn how it is measured and how it differs from email bounce rate.
A business development representative (BDR) prospects new accounts through outbound outreach and books sales meetings. Learn how a BDR differs from an SDR.
A buyer persona is a profile of the person who buys or influences a purchase. Learn how B2B buyer personas differ from an ICP and how they shape outreach.
Buying signals are events and behaviors that suggest a company may need a product soon, such as funding or hiring. Learn how B2B teams use buying signals.
A channel partner is a company that sells, resells or recommends another company's product to its own customers. Learn the main partner types.
Churn rate is the share of customers or revenue lost in a period. Learn how customer churn and revenue churn are calculated and why they differ.
Cold calling is phoning a potential buyer who has had no prior contact with the seller. Learn how B2B cold calling works and where it fits in outbound.
Cold email is a first, unsolicited email sent to a potential buyer with no prior relationship. Learn how B2B cold email works and what it depends on.
Competitive intelligence is gathering and analyzing public information about competitors to make better decisions. Learn how sales and marketing use it.
Content marketing is creating useful content that attracts and keeps a defined audience. Learn how B2B content marketing works and how it is measured.
Context engineering is designing everything a language model sees: instructions, examples, data, tool output and memory. Learn how it differs from prompts.
Conversion rate is the share of visitors or leads who complete a desired action. Learn the formula and how B2B teams use it across the funnel.
Conversion rate optimization (CRO) is the practice of raising the share of visitors who take a desired action. Learn how CRO testing works.
A CRM is the system where a company records its contacts, accounts, deals and every sales and marketing interaction. Learn what a CRM does in B2B.
Customer acquisition cost (CAC) is the total sales and marketing spend needed to win one new customer. Learn the CAC formula and how B2B teams use it.
Customer lifetime value (CLV or LTV) is the total value a customer brings over their relationship with a company. Learn how CLV is calculated and used.
Data enrichment adds missing details such as emails, titles and company size to your records from external sources. Learn how B2B data enrichment works.
Data hygiene is keeping CRM and marketing data accurate, complete and free of duplicates. Learn why B2B data decays and how teams keep it clean.
Deduplication (dedupe) finds records that describe the same person or company and merges them. Learn how dedupe works in CRM data and list building.
Demand generation builds awareness and interest in a target market before buyers are ready to buy. Learn how it differs from lead generation.
A discovery call is an early sales conversation to understand a prospect's situation, problems and buying process. Learn what a discovery call covers.
DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) adds a cryptographic signature to outgoing email so receivers can verify the sending domain. Learn how DKIM works.
DMARC is an email authentication policy that tells receiving servers how to handle mail failing SPF or DKIM checks. Learn how DMARC protects a domain.
Domain authority is a third-party score that estimates how well a website may rank based on its links. Learn what it measures and its limits.
An email bounce is a message that could not be delivered and was returned. Learn the difference between hard and soft bounces and why bounce rate matters.
Email deliverability is whether your email reaches the inbox instead of spam. Learn how authentication and sender reputation affect cold email.
An email finder is a tool that finds a person's likely work email from their name and company. Learn how email finders work and why verification matters.
Email verification checks whether an address exists and can receive mail before you send to it. Learn how email verification protects deliverability.
Email warmup is the practice of gradually raising sending volume from a new mailbox or domain to build sender reputation for cold email.
Firmographics are company attributes such as industry, headcount, revenue and location. Learn how B2B teams use firmographic data to segment accounts.
First-party data is information a company collects directly from its own audience and customers. Learn how it differs from second- and third-party data.
Generative engine optimization (GEO) is shaping content so AI search tools and assistants cite it in their answers. Learn how GEO differs from SEO.
Go-to-market (GTM) is the plan for how a company reaches buyers, sells to them and wins customers. Learn the parts of a B2B GTM strategy and motion.
GTM engineering is building automated go-to-market systems with code, APIs and AI: data, enrichment, signals, outreach and CRM sync. Learn what it covers.
Hyper-personalization is tailoring each message to the individual recipient using specific research. Learn how it differs from basic personalization.
An ideal customer profile (ICP) describes the companies that get the most from your product. Learn how to build one and how it differs from a persona.
An inbound lead is a potential buyer who contacts a company or shares details on their own initiative. Learn how inbound leads differ from outbound.
Intent data shows which companies are researching a topic and may be moving toward a purchase. Learn first, second and third-party intent.
Keyword research is finding the words buyers type into search engines and judging which ones to target. Learn how it works for B2B content and SEO.
A landing page is a web page built for one campaign and one action, such as a demo request. Learn how landing pages differ from home pages.
A large language model (LLM) is an AI model trained on large amounts of text to understand and generate language. Learn how LLMs are used in GTM.
Lead generation is the process of finding and attracting potential buyers and capturing their contact details. Learn how B2B lead generation works.
A lead magnet is a free resource offered in exchange for contact details. Learn how B2B teams use lead magnets on LinkedIn and websites to capture leads.
Lead nurturing is building a relationship with leads who are not ready to buy yet. Learn how B2B nurture sequences work and what they contain.
Lead qualification is deciding whether a lead is worth pursuing, based on fit, need and timing. Learn common criteria and frameworks such as BANT.
Lead scoring ranks leads by fit and engagement so sales works the best ones first. Learn how fit and behavior scores work and how lead scoring sets MQLs.
LinkedIn Ads are paid placements on LinkedIn targeted by job, company and audience data. Learn the main ad formats and how B2B teams use them.
LinkedIn InMail lets you message LinkedIn members you are not connected with, using credits from a premium plan. Learn how InMail works in B2B outreach.
LinkedIn Sales Navigator is LinkedIn's paid tool for sales prospecting, with advanced search, lead lists and alerts. Learn what it is used for.
LinkedIn Thought Leader Ads let a company promote posts written by its people as paid ads. Learn how they work and why B2B teams use them.
llms.txt is a proposed Markdown file at a website's root that gives AI agents a short overview and links to key content. Learn the format and its purpose.
Long-tail keywords are longer, more specific search phrases with lower volume and clearer intent. Learn why B2B teams target them and how to find them.
A lookalike audience is a group an ad platform builds to resemble a seed list, such as current customers. Learn how B2B teams use lookalikes.
Marketing automation is software that runs repetitive marketing tasks such as emails, lead scoring and routing on rules. Learn how B2B teams use it.
A marketing qualified lead (MQL) is a lead that meets marketing's fit and engagement criteria and is ready for sales. Learn how MQLs differ from SQLs.
Middle of funnel (MOFU) is the consideration stage, where buyers research ways to solve a problem. Learn what MOFU content and metrics look like.
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard for connecting AI applications to external tools and data. Learn how MCP servers and clients work.
Monthly recurring revenue (MRR) is the predictable subscription revenue a company earns each month. Learn how MRR is calculated and its parts.
Multi-touch attribution splits credit for a conversion across several touchpoints. Learn the common models and the limits of multi-touch attribution.
An MX record is the DNS entry that tells sending servers where to deliver email for a domain. Learn how MX records work and why they matter for cold email.
Net revenue retention (NRR) measures how much recurring revenue a company keeps and grows from existing customers. Learn the NRR formula and its meaning.
Outbound sales is when the seller starts the conversation with buyers who have not reached out. Learn how outbound differs from inbound and what it uses.
Paid media is any marketing channel where a company pays for placement, such as search, social and display ads. Learn how B2B teams use paid media.
Personal branding is how a professional builds a reputation for specific expertise. Learn how founders and B2B leaders use it on LinkedIn.
Pipeline generation is creating qualified sales opportunities that can turn into revenue. Learn how B2B teams build and measure pipeline generation.
Product-led growth (PLG) is a go-to-market motion where the product itself drives signups, adoption and expansion. Learn how PLG works in B2B software.
Programmatic SEO is building many search-targeted pages from a template and a dataset. Learn when it works and how to keep the pages useful.
Prompt engineering is writing and refining instructions so an AI model produces useful, reliable output. Learn the basics and how it fits with context.
Reverse IP lookup matches an IP address to the domain or organization behind it. Learn how B2B teams use it to identify companies visiting their site.
RevOps (revenue operations) runs the systems, data and processes behind marketing, sales and customer success as one function. Learn what RevOps teams own.
A sales cycle is the series of steps and the time it takes to turn a prospect into a customer. Learn how B2B teams measure sales cycle length.
A sales development representative (SDR) prospects and qualifies leads, then books meetings for account executives. Learn what an SDR does in B2B sales.
A sales engagement platform runs multi-step outreach sequences across email, calls and LinkedIn and tracks the results. Learn what these tools do.
A sales forecast is an estimate of the revenue a team expects to close in a period. Learn common forecasting methods and how forecast accuracy is judged.
A sales lead is a person or company that may become a customer. Learn how leads differ from prospects and opportunities, and the main lead stages.
A sales pipeline is the set of open deals organized by stage, from first meeting to closed. Learn how pipeline stages work and how teams manage them.
A sales playbook is a written guide to how a team sells: who it targets, what it says and how deals progress. Learn what a sales playbook contains.
Sales prospecting is finding and contacting potential buyers who fit your ideal customer profile. Learn the main prospecting methods in B2B sales.
A sales qualified lead (SQL) is a prospect sales has reviewed and accepted as a real opportunity. Learn how SQLs differ from MQLs.
Win rate is the share of sales opportunities that end in a closed won deal. Learn how to calculate win rate and how win-loss analysis improves it.
Search engine optimization (SEO) is improving a website so it ranks in unpaid search results. Learn the main parts of SEO and how it relates to GEO.
Search intent is the goal behind a search query. Learn the four common types of search intent and why matching it matters for SEO and content.
Serviceable addressable market (SAM) is the part of the total market a company can actually serve today. Learn how SAM relates to TAM and SOM.
Social listening monitors social platforms and communities for mentions of a brand, competitor or topic. Learn how B2B teams turn it into timely outreach.
Social selling is using social networks, mainly LinkedIn, to find, understand and build relationships with buyers. Learn how B2B social selling works.
Speed to lead is how quickly a company responds after a lead raises their hand. Learn why response time matters and how teams shorten it.
An SPF record is a DNS TXT record listing the servers allowed to send email for a domain. Learn how SPF checks work and affect cold email delivery.
Spintax is a text format like {Hi|Hello} that lets sending tools vary a message for each recipient. Learn how spintax works in cold email.
Stakeholder mapping identifies everyone involved in a B2B purchase and their role and influence. Learn how sales teams map buying committees.
Technographics describe the software and technologies a company uses. Learn how B2B teams use technographic data to segment and prioritize accounts.
Third-party data is information collected by outside providers and sold or licensed to companies. Learn how B2B teams use it and what to check.
Top of funnel (TOFU) is the awareness stage, where potential buyers first learn about a problem or a company. Learn what TOFU content and metrics look like.
Total addressable market (TAM) is the full revenue opportunity for a product. Learn how to size TAM bottom up and how it relates to SAM and SOM.
A trigger event is a change at an account, such as new funding or a new leader, that can create a reason to buy. Learn how sales teams use them.
UTM parameters are tags added to a URL that tell analytics tools which source, medium and campaign sent a visitor. Learn the five core UTM parameters.
Waterfall enrichment queries several data providers in sequence until one returns a result. Learn how waterfall enrichment raises email and phone coverage.
Web scraping is automatically extracting data from web pages into a structured format. Learn how GTM teams use web scraping for lists and research.
Workflow automation is using software to run a sequence of business steps on rules and triggers. Learn how sales and marketing teams use it.
